focus: Actual symptom tonight across a UTC/local-date boundary
reason: A current evening narrative establishes the patient-local date even when the received timestamp has advanced to the next UTC date.

focus: Evening occurrence with a limited-window count
reason: An evening interval anchors today but does not turn a game-time count into a cumulative or completed-day total.

focus: Negated evening symptoms and bounded absence
reason: Explicit evening absence is dated locally; a rehearsal-specific vomiting zero covers the rehearsal rather than the whole day.

focus: Conditional vomiting tonight
reason: A contingency plan mentions a symptom on the current evening without asserting that it has happened or supplying a count.

focus: Actual tonight symptoms, clock time, and medication sequence
reason: Two actual evening symptoms have distinct evidence; only the expressly timed episode gets a clock time, and the medication relation belongs to nausea.

focus: Ordinary morning and afternoon anchors
reason: Separate daytime activities support the same local date without supporting invented clock times or a whole-day vomiting total.

focus: Known historical morning with an unknown count
reason: Repeated vomiting establishes occurrence within an anchored window but supplies no exact episode count.

focus: Undated meal window
reason: A meal supplies a bounded context while the explicitly lost date prevents assignment to the submission day.

focus: Uncertain numerical alternatives for a daily count
reason: A choice between two possible counts is not an exact count; the daily scope and confirmed occurrence remain usable.

focus: A combined count across four explicitly listed dates
reason: A single tally combines four named dates without a daily allocation, so the bounded count stays a window with an unsupported single-date representation.

focus: Explicit historical date and exact clock time
reason: A dated log entry identifies a particular episode, independent of the later submission date.

focus: Explicit completed-day total of zero
reason: Full-day absence on a completed historical date is a day total; interval boundaries do not identify an event at midnight.

focus: Unsupported scale with compatible severity context
reason: The daily maximum is explicit, but an eight on a ten-point scale must not be converted into the fixed five-point trend.

focus: A five-point rating elicited for the instant of a call
reason: The explicitly momentary question makes a selected numeric rating ineligible for the worst-so-far-today trend; the call supplies no exact clock time.

focus: Known date but unspecified severity summary context
reason: A today label and five-point number do not establish whether the score is a maximum or a current measurement.

focus: Conflicting positive daily counts at a timezone boundary
reason: Compatible text and form counts disagree on number while both confirm occurrence; today follows the patient-local date.

focus: Valid structured rating alongside unsupported text scale
reason: The form independently supplies an eligible severity; an incompatible text scale remains a diagnostic rather than a conflict between eligible scores.

focus: Exact event distinct from a questionnaire daily total
reason: One clock-timed episode and a larger form total have incompatible scopes and must remain separate observations rather than a count conflict.

focus: Multiple symptoms with separate dates and absence
reason: Historical nausea and current absence are distinct claims; a zero vomiting tally adds only the explicitly denied symptom for today.

focus: Irrelevant administrative text
reason: An administrative message contains neither target symptom and must not create symptom observations or inferred absence.
